title: The Akhand Kirtani Jatha
hook: a movement known for all-night kirtan and strict discipline

segments.voice: Yesterday, santhiaa, teacher reads and student repeats, and your line was sound it right. Today, a stream that sings all night.

It's past midnight in a hall with the lights turned low. Most of the city is asleep. On the floor, rows of people sit cross-legged, some swaying a little, some with eyes closed. A harmonium starts a line, and the whole room sings it back. Then again. Then a new verse. Nobody checks the time. Hours later, a gray light comes through the high windows, and the singing is still going. People call this a rainsabaee, a night that lasts the whole night. A group known for it is today's stream.
screen: `PAST MIDNIGHT, LIGHTS LOW.` → `THE ROOM SINGS IT BACK.` → `STILL SINGING AT FIRST LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Take the name apart. Akhand means unbroken. Kirtani means those who do kirtan, the singing of the Guru's hymns. Jatha means a band, a company that moves together. So: the company of unbroken singing. Tradition traces the group to Bhai Randhir Singh, a Sikh remembered for long hours of devotion and a strict life. Two things mark the Jatha. The first is kirtan itself. Its programs often run through the night, in a plain, congregational style. The sangat doesn't only listen; it sings, repeating lines together until the repetition becomes a kind of breathing. Members speak of that late, shared singing as a way the Name settles into a person. The second is discipline. The Jatha is known for keeping the rehat strictly, and some members keep observances beyond the common code, in diet and daily practice. Not every Sikh sees those extra observances the same way, and that question is left to the panth. What the Jatha leans on comes from the Granth. Guru Arjan, in Raag Maru on Ang 1075, says in paraphrase that in this dark age, singing the Lord's praise is the foremost thing. Kirtan isn't decoration on the side of worship; in that line, it stands at the front. And why the night? Gurbani speaks of the amrit vela, the ambrosial hours before dawn, as a time for the Name. A night of kirtan walks straight into those hours instead of waking up for them. Few people can give a whole night to anything, but the shape still teaches: a song kept going long enough stops being a performance and becomes a place you live for a while.
screen: `AKHAND KIRTANI JATHA: THE UNBROKEN SINGERS.` · `KIRTAN: THE SANGAT SINGS TOGETHER.` · `DISCIPLINE: THE REHAT KEPT STRICTLY.` · `ANG 1075: KIRTAN STANDS AT THE FRONT.` · then, large: `KIRTAN TILL DAWN.`

segments.voice: If you have a recording of Gurbani kirtan, put it on quietly; if not, simply listen to the room. Let one repeated line or sound carry your breath in and out, without trying to follow every word, and if you pray, rest on Waheguru between the lines.
The Akhand Kirtani Jatha. A Sikh company known for kirtan that runs through the night, and for keeping the rehat strictly. Akhand: unbroken. Today's word.
Your line: kirtan till dawn. The singers reach the amrit vela already singing. See you in the morning.

It's a contest, and whoever sings the longest becomes the group's new leader.
